concepts.way: misconception: local variables get a default value on their own
concepts.quote: int c; declares c, so c is 0.
concepts.why: A local declared without an initializer is unassigned, not 0; reading c + 1 is a compile error, so the stated rule contradicts Java.
The answer says nothing about int's range, arithmetic or type behaviour beyond naming it in the declaration.

concepts.way: everyday_reading: novices think int x; already sets x to 0
concepts.why: It treats declaring a local variable as giving it a value, contradicting the rule that a local must be assigned before it is read.
